summary: Frontend-only verification of driver-side counter-offer + countdown UX (iter88). Driver login (api), /chauffeur/home, online toggle, incoming-request-modal, counter-offer→my-offer-panel with CountdownRing/amount/status, renew reset, and passenger-side /taxi-bidding regression. Core driver counter-offer UX + countdown ticking + renew RESET all VERIFIED. Driver→active ride transition could not be fully verified end-to-end via UI in second run due to test pollution (modal showed a different (priority/TIER2) pending ride than the one created), but backend counter-offer payload (expires_at + ttl_seconds) and ride.counter_offers list with expires_at confirmed via API.

minor.issue: Returns 404 — no dedicated offers list endpoint. Offers are only embedded in GET /api/rides/{ride_id} as ride.counter_offers. Not blocking (UI uses ride object), but noteworthy if any consumer expects it.

integration_issues.flow: Driver→active ride transition after passenger accepts our offer
integration_issues.issue: Could not be deterministically verified in 2nd run because the incoming-request-modal sometimes surfaces a stale/priority pending ride (not the ride created seconds earlier by the test passenger), causing the UI counter-offer POST to 404. Likely cross-test data pollution (multiple pending rides queued from prior iterations). The polling logic in DriverHome.js looks correct (ride.driver_id === driver.id → setCurrentRide).

verified_scenarios: Driver session via /api/auth/login → cookies applied → /chauffeur/home loads (driver-home-page visible).
online-toggle switches Hors ligne → En ligne.
Passenger creates pending ride via POST /api/rides (payment_method='cash' required) → driver incoming-request-modal renders within 8s poll (PASS).

Driver types into counter-offer-input (15.50), clicks send-counter-offer-btn → my-offer-panel appears with my-offer-amount=15.50 EUR, my-offer-status='Expire dans 29s · en attente du client', offer-countdown ring visible (PASS).
renew-offer-btn click resets countdown back to 28s (PASS, my-offer-status updates).

Backend POST /api/rides/{id}/counter-offer returns 200 with offer.id, offer.expires_at, offer.ttl_seconds; GET /api/rides/{id} returns ride.counter_offers[0].expires_at populated (backend wiring confirmed).
unverified_scenarios: Final driver UI transition to current-ride after passenger calls /accept-offer/{offer_id}: in 1st run the modal showed the test-created ride and counter-offer succeeded; in 2nd run the modal showed a TIER-2 priority ride (different ride_id) so the UI counter-offer 404'd before transition could be exercised. Recommended: main agent self-test by purging pending rides before run, OR have driver-side click accept-ride-btn on the test-created ride only. Logic in DriverHome.js useEffect on myOffer (poll + ride.driver_id===driver.id check) looks correct.

Passenger /taxi-bidding offer cards with CountdownRing: page renders the request form, but offers are only displayed when the page itself holds the `searching` rideId state (set after submitting from this page). Visiting /taxi-bidding fresh after creating rides via API does NOT show offer-countdown elements (count=0). This is by design (no persisted searching state) — not a regression.
action_items: MAIN AGENT: Verify the final transition (passenger accept-offer → driver sees current-ride) manually or by ensuring no stale pending rides leak across test runs. The UI code path looks correct; this is a test-data hygiene issue, not a code bug.
OPTIONAL: Consider exposing GET /api/rides/{ride_id}/offers (currently 404) — would help SDET and frontend code that wants offers-only without full ride payload.

OPTIONAL: When multiple pending rides exist, DriverHome.loadPendingRides only surfaces res.data[0]. If a priority WS message fires for a different ride afterward it overrides incomingRequest — could cause UI/intent mismatches as observed here. Consider deduplicating by ride.id or preferring the test-created ride first by created_at.
critical_code_review_comments: DriverHome.js sendCounterOffer uses raw fetch; on non-200 it only logs to console and leaves the input modal up — user gets no toast/error feedback. Add a visible error toast on failure.
DriverHome.js counter-offer input uses document.getElementById(`counter-input-${incomingRequest.id}`) to read value rather than React state — works but is anti-pattern; refactor to useState.
The 30s timer is computed only from expires_at; if the device clock drifts vs server, countdown may be off. Acceptable but worth a future server-driven ttl_seconds remaining approach.

WebSocket fails in preview (wss errors logged). The 8s poll fallback works, but the driver-side priority_ride_offer subscription is effectively dead in preview — confirm production has the WS reachable.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (5/6 sub-flows verified; transition step blocked by test data pollution, not a code bug)

seed_data_creation: Two pending rides were created during the test (ride_d6320e6a7b35, ride_0420c75fe4ad and an earlier ride_659f21f7c29a in first run). They remain in 'pending' status — recommend cleanup before re-running.
context_for_next_testing_agent: POST /api/rides REQUIRES payment_method (e.g. 'cash') in addition to vehicle_type and proposed_fare or you'll get 422. Offers are NOT exposed at /api/rides/{id}/offers (404); instead read GET /api/rides/{id} → ride.counter_offers (each item has id, driver_id, amount, status, expires_at). Pending rides accumulate across runs and the driver modal surfaces res.data[0] from /api/rides?status=pending — purge old pending rides if you want determinism. WS is down in preview; rely on 8s poll for incoming and 2.5s for my-offer.
rca_of_the_issue: No code bug found in the new counter-offer/CountdownRing/renew UX — all elements (my-offer-panel, my-offer-amount, my-offer-status, offer-countdown, renew-offer-btn, cancel-offer-btn) render correctly with proper data-testids, the 30s timer renders & ticks, and renew resets it. The only unverified piece (driver auto-transition into currentRide) is blocked by orchestration noise from cross-iteration pending rides, not by the feature code.
